title: slop-lint config
description: slop-lint.config.json. Command-line flags win over every value here.

lang.description: Language of the text when --lang is not given.

format.description: How every file is read when --format is not given. Left out, a .md file is Markdown and anything else is text.

anchors.description: Extra anchor terms, such as tool names written in lowercase. --anchors replaces them.

ignore.description: Files that are skipped even when named on the command line.

overrides.description: Settings for the files that match. Every matching entry applies, in order, so a later one wins.

level.description: 1 banned: reported and the run fails. 2 reported, the run passes. 3 context word: passes in a sentence with an anchor, otherwise joins the Tier 2 budget.

severity.description: What the finding costs the score: disqualify sets it to 0, high 3 points, medium 1.5, low 0.5.

glob.description: A path pattern relative to the folder of the config file, with forward slashes. * stays inside one path segment, ? is one character, ** crosses folders. No braces, classes or negation, no leading ./ and no trailing slash.

ruleSettings.description: Per rule id: "off", or a new level, severity or both. The id is a built-in rule's or a custom rule's.

id.description: Starts with X-, so it can never take the id of a built-in rule.

name.description: Short name for --list-rules and SARIF. The id when left out.

message.description: What is wrong, shown with every finding.

pattern.description: JavaScript regex source. It must compile and must not match the empty string. Its running time is yours to keep in check: there is no time limit.

flags.description: Any of g, i, m, s, u, each once. "giu" when left out; g and u are always added.

suppressions.description: How the inline directives of Markdown mode behave.

allowDisqualify.description: Lets a directive suppress a rule whose severity is disqualify. Default false.

mask.description: Honors the directives without a rule id, which hide a span from every rule. Default true.

failOnProblems.description: Exit 1 on an unused, refused or invalid directive. Default false.
